analysis.title: Persistent tech pressures underline need for portfolio resilience
key_insights: Tech sold off hard on Friday. Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% and S&P 500 fell 3.7%, its seventh straight decline. Nasdaq is 19.8% below its 6 October high, near bear-market territory.
S&P 500 is in correction, down 11.5% since 6 October. VIX reached nearly 36, the highest since the spring 2025 Liberation Day tariff turmoil.

Selling reflects doubts on AI infrastructure spending sustainability given physical and financing constraints, and whether AI revenues justify the investment. NVIDIA leadership transition and a WSJ report of an SEC civil probe added uncertainty.

Markets price near-100% odds of a 25bp Fed hike in December with more tightening expected in Q1. Fed communications are hawkish, with two Governors among those backing more tightening, and October minutes flagged broadening inflation pressures.
Treasuries rallied, with the 10-year yield down 10bp to 4.95%.

Gold fell to a 14-month low of USD 3,518/oz and was down about 9% on the week on higher real rates, a stronger dollar and possible liquidation to cover losses elsewhere. Copper is on track for its steepest weekly fall since April 2025 as the AI trade reassessment spread to data-center beneficiaries.

UBS base case for 2027 is near-trend growth, rising earnings, higher AI investment and moderating inflation later in the year. Risk-reward is now more balanced and global equities were recently downgraded from Attractive to Neutral.

US tech AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by end-2028. UBS estimates AI model and application revenues need to reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return, and gains will be uneven.

Investors are advised to keep a long-term view, diversify, and maintain shopping and disposal lists with predefined add and sell levels. Risk-averse investors may rebalance into high-quality bonds, while patient investors may look at the sharpest-decline areas.

Equity preferences: about 15% 2027 earnings growth forecast in both US and Eurozone, Eurozone preferred region, favor industrials and health care, and US equal-weight to cut tech concentration. Within AI, favor financially strong hyperscalers and selected compute, foundry, semicap and infrastructure software leaders.
Structured strategies may help investors participate or earn income while implied volatility is elevated, with sizing caveats on capital-loss, issuer, liquidity and opportunity-cost risks.

Gold forecast is USD 5,000/oz by December 2027 and a strategic allocation is maintained. Copper remains the preferred industrial metal, and UBS favors actively managed energy, industrial metals, agriculture and precious metals.
